established: The adapter delegates to the original Memory owner rather than duplicating mutation logic.
Each write opens and closes its own original Memory owner before returning; successful and rejected duplicate writes leave no owned live writer lock.
A settled receipt verifies immutable original revision bytes, record hash, reserved one-use intent, exact operation/library/entry/revision identities and committed-index reachability.
Known save/revise receipts remain verifiable after forgetting; verification returns only acknowledgement metadata, not historical text.
An unknown existing writer lock is not stolen or removed; read-only verification of a previously settled receipt remains possible.
Write bindings expose verifyResult; selected intentDigest binds exact immutable authority descriptors independently of input order.
boundaries: These are adapter tests, not proof that the Runtime resumed an unfinished Run; the Runtime fault-injection qualification is separate.
No reconciliation of an unknown mid-write operation is implemented. A file or intent reservation alone is not a successful Runtime receipt.
File publication and SQLite checkpoints are separate systems, not one transaction or a generic exactly-once guarantee.
No lock theft, new grant creation, raw-log publication, model call, remote change or formal release occurred.
